system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Current code in view: [The currently opened file, specified by the latest call of the view tool.]
system_prompt_style.note: Paper only; system prompt includes per-step state (code in view, breakpoints, last eval output, last observation) and tool instructions.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Repo directory tree: [Visible files in the repository, presented in the form of a directory tree. This is controlled by the .debugignore file.]
env_context_strategy.note: Directory tree (depth 1 default) injected plus view/listdir/pdb tools for navigation.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: History of command and terminal outputs (the last 20 steps):
context_compaction.note: Sliding window of last 20 steps in example agents.

observation_format.evidence_quote: debug-gym represents observation information in structured text (e.g., JSON format) and defines a simple syntax for text actions

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: The meta-syntax adopts the triple-backtick delimiter ``` from Markdown.
tool_call_format.note: Closest value: delimiter-based text parsing using triple backticks, not XML tags. Paper v1 only; no repo evidence.

tool_count.note: Paper lists 5 built-in tools (eval, view, pdb, rewrite, listdir); the default count depends on user-registered agent config, which the paper does not fix.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: our rewrite tool takes a file path, a pair of start and end line numbers, and the new content as input; it will replace the code between the start and end lines
edit_primitive.note: Without line numbers the tool rewrites the whole file.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: An instructions attribute, which is a dictionary containing information about the tool that will be visible to the agent

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: By default, this tool is automatically triggered after a rewrite action, but this can be modified by the user through configuration.
loop_primitives.note: Step loop in Sec. 2.2; eval auto-run after rewrite.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Output a single command, nothing else.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: We provide three example agents with debug-gym to showcase its API, all of which are LLM-based agents with minimal architectural design

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: We provide three example agents with debug-gym to showcase its API, all of which are LLM-based agents with minimal architectural design

human_in_loop.note: Paper says agents may include humans-in-the-loop but no gating mechanism described.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: We keep a list of all breakpoints and restore them when there is a terminal session restarts.
short_term_state.note: Env tracks current file, breakpoints, last eval output.

self_verification.evidence_quote: By default, this tool is automatically triggered after a rewrite action

retry_policy.note: Experiments run three times for statistics, not retry.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: An episode is terminated when either an agent has received a positive reward (success), or it has exhausted a pre-defined budget, in the form of the number of steps or the number of consumed tokens
termination_condition.note: Rewrite budget (10) also used in experiments.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: it has exhausted a pre-defined budget, in the form of the number of steps or the number of consumed tokens (out of budget)

timeouts.evidence_quote: Despite having a timeout defined in debug-gym's eval tool, this only captures infinite loops or extremely slow cases.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: debug-gym will copy the user-specified repository into a temporary working directory, which is by default mapped into a Docker container.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: Users can additionally specify read only files or directories using a .debugreadonly file
filesystem_access.note: .debugignore and .debugreadonly restrict scope inside the container.

tracing.note: Paper analyzes experimental logs/trajectories but format not described.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: we integrate three coding benchmarks into debug-gym to quantitatively measure LLM-based agents' performance in interactive debugging

guardrails.evidence_quote: the read only setting can prevent agents from developing cheating strategies such as to pass the tests by editing or deleting them.

target_domain.evidence_quote: we present a textual environment, namely debug-gym, for developing LLM-based agents in an interactive coding setting.

open_source.evidence_quote: We open source debug-gym at aka.ms/debug-gym.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: For closed-weights LLMs, we query them through online APIs, for open-weights ones, we host them using vLLM

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: this technical report describes debug-gym, an interactive coding environment
primary_artifact.note: Only paper evidence available; no pinned repo evidence.

first_release_date.note: Paper v1 dated 27 Mar 2025 (arXiv:2503.21557v1); no tag evidence.
